lesson_title: Two Families, Same Needs, Different Ladders
hook_text: Two families have exactly the same needs. So why does one stop halfway up the ladder?
clip_script: Picture a ladder. Bottom rungs: food, water, shelter, clothes. Those are primary needs, you need them first to stay alive. Middle rungs: school costs, transport, a phone, a fridge. Secondary needs, they make life better. Top rungs: takeaways, subscriptions, savings. Wants. Family one earns R4 000 a month. Maize meal, rent, paraffin, taxi fares, and the money is gone, halfway up the ladder. Family two earns R30 000. Bottom and middle sorted, takeaway on Friday, savings in the bank. Same needs. The difference is income. That is why jobs, and free services like clinics and no-fee schools, change a family's whole life.
visual_style: A whiteboard ladder with rungs labelled primary, secondary and wants, and two stick-figure families climbing to different heights.
mood: Thoughtful and fair, comparing without judging.
pacing: A steady climb rung by rung, then a split-screen comparison.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort ten things in your home into primary, secondary or want.
